To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the endogenization of input coefficients has a strong impact on the results, that the endogenized input coefficients are more sensitive to changes in output than in input prices, and that the endogenous coefficients show less variation than their exogenous counterparts.

the input–output price equations are consistent with a cost function approach; the cost function approach allows the estimation of the price elasticities of demand; the cost function can be used to estimate the technical coefficients; the technical coefficients can be estimated by using a cost function approach.

(1) the endogenized model performs better than the traditional model in the sense that the former has a higher R2 and a lower root mean square error; (2) the endogenization of the model is not a mere statistical exercise; it has a clear economic meaning, and it can be used for policy purposes; and (3) the model can be used for forecasting purposes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a model of the demand side of a small open economy.
the following question: what are the implications of an endogenized technical coefficient matrix on the price system?
the interplay between the supply side (the cost function) and the demand side (the input–output model).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the endogenization of the technical coefficients is a useful and promising extension to the standard input–output model and that it is worthwhile to continue the development of the endogenization approach.
the model is a step in the right direction, although it is not the ultimate solution to the problem of endogenizing technical coefficients.

the endogenous input–output model provides a better description of economic reality than its exogenous counterpart, although the latter has a more direct relation to the input–output tables and their use in economic planning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the endogenization of input prices is a necessary step in the econometric estimation of input–output models.
the model is able to explain the behaviour of the Dutch economy over the 1971-1986 period in a reasonable way.

the endogenization of intermediate demand and labour supply has a significant effect on the estimated parameters of the price equations, and that this effect is larger than the effects found by other studies that have endogenized only the intermediate demand.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the input–output model can be extended to a model in which input and output prices and factor demands are simultaneously determined.
a simple endogenization of the technical coefficients in an input–output framework is possible.
the endogenization of the technical coefficients in the input–output framework can be done in several ways, each with a different focus and with different implications.
